answer: Reputation Decay Surcharge Curve. Each new identity starts at a kernel reputation weight; every action's cost scales as (1/reputation)^1.5, so fresh sybils pay a steep premium until activity history accumulates. Interacting with a lotus-tagged cluster of low-age peers applies an additional multiplier, capping the discount a farm can reach. Attacker cost per sustained identity rises superlinearly toward a summit at which marginal identities cost more than the value they extract, so only dense legitimate histories clear the curve.
